question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{24}∼N(-5,{12}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $24$ from a normal population, calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.6).$

*Hint: A value table of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.0\,$ | $\,0.5160\,$ | $\,0.5199\,$ | $\,0.5239\,$ |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ | $\,0.5596\,$ | $\,0.5636\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ | $\,0.5987\,$ | $\,0.6026\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(-5,\frac{{12}^{2}}{24}) \\  & ∼N(-5,6).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.6).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.6) & =P(Z<\frac{-4.6-(-5)}{\sqrt{6}}) \\  & =P(Z<0.16) \\  & =Φ(0.16)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.16)=0.5636.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<-4.6) & =Φ(0.16) \\  & =0.5636.\end{aligned}
$$
